response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT BillingState, COUNT(*) AS c FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingState), s AS (SELECT c, c * 1.0 / SUM(c) OVER () AS share, AVG(c * 1.0) OVER () AS avg_c FROM g) SELECT SUM(c) AS total_invoices, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(c - avg_c) AS avg_excess FROM s WHERE c > avg_c

assumptions.assumption: Invoices with a NULL BillingState form one group. GROUP BY already puts NULLs together, so no special handling is needed. Empty-string states are not treated as missing.

The average count per group is taken over all groups, including the NULL-state group. It is computed before the above-average filter is applied. Shares use the total of all invoices as the denominator.
